questions.stem: What is the circuit symbol for a variable resistor?

options.text: Two parallel lines of different length
A circle with a cross inside
A rectangle with an arrow through it
A rectangle with a line through it

questions.explanation: A variable resistor is represented by a rectangle (the standard resistor symbol) with an arrow drawn through it, indicating that its resistance can be changed.

questions.stem: What is the difference between a cell and a battery in circuit diagrams?

options.text: A cell is a single unit of chemical energy; a battery is two or more cells connected together
There is no difference; the terms are interchangeable
A cell provides AC while a battery provides DC
A battery is always rechargeable but a cell is not

questions.explanation: A cell is a single source of electrical energy (shown as one long and one short parallel line). A battery consists of two or more cells connected together in series.

questions.stem: Which component allows current to flow in only one direction?

options.text: Fuse
Capacitor
Diode
Resistor

questions.explanation: A diode only allows current to flow in one direction (forward bias). Its circuit symbol is a triangle pointing towards a line, and current flows in the direction the triangle points.

questions.stem: What is the function of a fuse in a circuit?

options.text: To measure the voltage across a component
To break the circuit if the current exceeds a safe value by melting
To store electrical energy
To increase the current in the circuit

questions.explanation: A fuse is a safety device containing a thin wire that melts and breaks the circuit if the current becomes too large, protecting the circuit and its components from damage.

questions.stem: Which component emits light when a current flows through it in the forward direction?

options.text: Transformer
Light-dependent resistor (LDR)
Light-emitting diode (LED)
Thermistor

questions.explanation: A light-emitting diode (LED) emits light when current flows through it in the forward direction. Unlike a filament lamp, an LED requires very little current and produces almost no heat.

questions.stem: What does a thermistor do in a circuit?

options.text: It changes its resistance in response to temperature changes
It generates heat to warm the circuit
It converts light energy into electrical energy
It stores charge and releases it later

questions.explanation: A thermistor is a resistor whose resistance changes significantly with temperature. An NTC thermistor has a resistance that decreases as temperature increases, making it useful as a temperature sensor.

questions.stem: How is an ammeter connected in a circuit to measure current?

options.text: It can be connected in any arrangement
Between the two terminals of the battery only
In parallel with the component
In series with the component

questions.explanation: An ammeter must be connected in series with the component so that the same current flows through both the ammeter and the component. It has a very low resistance to avoid affecting the circuit.
